title: Music & Marketing — Karas ir Taika
text: Karas ir Taika "War and Peace", a new album split into a War side and a Peace side. I was its art department and back office at once: I arranged the photoshoot with photographer T. Terekas, designed the cover, gatefold and centre labels around its contact sheet of film photos, then took it all the way to the Green Lakes Pressing vinyl factory and onto the merch table. Read more Behind the artwork sat everything else a record needs: print-ready files, proofs and pressing deadlines with the factory, the budget and a LATGA grant I secured, contracts and 300 hand-numbered copies. I also made sure the audio arrived in the right shape, arranging masters from sound engineer Pavel Daniels to the technical standards of both vinyl cutting and CD replication. The album also came out on CD, with 500 copies produced in the Netherlands. I opened a pre-sale on the band's website and arranged a five-concert tour around the release, in Vilnius, Kaunas, Klaipėda, Alytus and Ukmergė. The vinyl edition is now nearly sold out, and a second pressing is planned for the near future. title: Music & Marketing — Niekam nežinomi žmonės
text:
Niekam nežinomi žmonės
The band's 1998 debut, remastered and pressed on vinyl for the first time as a gift to longtime fans. It had only ever existed on cassette and CD, so I rebuilt the original artwork as a gatefold for the new format and managed the reissue from master to marbled vinyl.
Read more
The original cover was created by the well-known Lithuanian artist Saulius Urbonavičius-Samas, with photos by Claudia Reichardt. My job was to respect it: I kept as much of the design as possible and reworked it to fit a 12-inch gatefold and new centre labels.
I arranged the remastering of the original 1998 recordings with sound engineer Pavel Daniels, then took the record to the Green Lakes Pressing vinyl factory, in black and in turquoise marble. Around it I handled the licences and paperwork a reissue needs, and opened a pre-sale on the band's website.
The launch shows sold out, two concerts back to back. At the release, DJ Mamania of G&G Sindikatas put it simply: "one of the best Lithuanian rock albums".

title: Music & Marketing — Senos naujienos
text: Senos naujienos "Old News", the album Requiem never made. Around 2003 the band planned a new record that never happened, and its songs stayed scattered as singles or went unreleased. I collected ten of them into the album they should have been, and built the whole idea around the headlines they made at the time. Read more Among them is the hit "Aš nupirksiu tau namą", which helped win the band the title of best rock band two years in a row and stayed in the radio charts for an incredibly long time: 33 weeks on Radiocentras. The concept and design are mine. I dug up old articles and photos from newspapers and magazines, mostly from the early 2000s, and turned them into a real newspaper called Senos naujienos . Band leader Tomas Krivickas reads it on the cover, and the full paper is printed on the record's inner sleeve. Some songs were remastered and some freshly recorded, including a new version of Skandalas with the well-known Lithuanian artist ba. (Benas Aleksandravičius), recorded with sound engineer Pavel Daniels at Rockmergė records. Behind it I ran the budget, the recording sessions, the master files and the licences, then took it to Green Lakes Pressing and launched it with concerts in Ukmergė and Vilnius. The problem
I managed releases for a rock band for years, and every single one meant the same scramble: when to pitch Spotify editorial, which radio stations to email, what to post and on which day. Independent artists rarely have a manager to plan this, so good songs come out with no plan at all.

title: DropOperator case study — What I built
text:
What I built
Song in, strategy out. Upload an MP3/WAV or paste a YouTube URL. The app transcribes the lyrics, detects the genre and builds a release plan with dates.
A LangGraph ReAct agent with 6 tools decides what it needs: audio analysis, lyrics, Spotify data, and a Pinecone RAG knowledge base of music-marketing know-how (512 chunks).
Plans become work. Every step syncs into a calendar and a to-do board in Supabase. Each task has its own assistant for writing Spotify pitches, radio emails and captions.
Beyond single releases: concert and social-campaign project types, band profiles and per-project memory.

title: ReviewReply case study
text:
← AI Engineering / Case study 02
ReviewReply .
A Chrome extension that drafts on-brand replies to Google Business reviews, in one click, right inside Google's review page.
Role
Solo: product, code and prompts
Built for
A real bar client, made reusable
Year
2026 · v0.2.1
Cost
A fraction of a cent per reply
The problem
Small businesses get the same kinds of reviews again and again: a long wait at the bar, a refused entry, a wrong bill, praise for a favourite bartender. Answering each one well takes time, and generic AI replies sound generic. I was answering reviews for a bar client myself and wanted something that answers the way the owner would.

title: ReviewReply case study — What I built
text:
What I built
A situations playbook. For every recurring situation, the business describes how to recognise it, how to respond and what never to say. The model picks the matching situation and shows which one it used.
One-click drafts on the page. A "✨ Draft reply" bar above each reply box, with Shorter , Warmer and Try again .
Profiles and templates for bars, restaurants, cafés, hotels and salons, with JSON import and export.
Safe by default. Rules stop the AI admitting liability, promising refunds or repeating personal details. Review text is treated as data, never as instructions, and it's tested against a built-in "ignore previous instructions" attack.
Human in the loop. The extension only types a draft. A person reads it and clicks Google's own Post button.
No server. The API key stays in the browser, and reviews go only to OpenAI.

title: Fake News Detection case study — Pipeline
text:
Pipeline
Cleaning: NLTK normalisation, stop-word removal and Snowball stemming.
Features: TF-IDF on 1–2-grams (min_df 5, max_df 0.8) plus FastText word embeddings.
Models: Logistic Regression, Multinomial Naive Bayes, Random Forest and SVM, compared on the same validation split.
Ensemble: a probability-averaging hybrid of NB + LR + FastText beat every single model.

title: Customer Feedback Intelligence case study
text:
← AI Engineering / Case study 04
Customer Feedback Intelligence .
"Because reading 34,000 reviews manually is not data science. It's punishment." An NLP pipeline that turns raw Amazon reviews into sentiment, product groups and summaries a business can act on.
Team
Pavitra & Rima
Context
Ironhack AI Engineering
Year
2026
Data
34,620 Amazon reviews
Project presentation · use ← → or swipe
What it does
Classify sentiment. Star ratings mapped to three classes and balanced (812 per class). Text prepared with stemming, negation handling ("not_good") and TF-IDF bigrams, then labelled with VADER and a RoBERTa sentiment model (cardiffnlp twitter-roberta-base).
Group products. Sentence-Transformer embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) clustered with K-Means . The elbow method chose k = 5, shown with PCA, and each cluster got a business-friendly name like "Top-Rated & Premium Picks".
Summarise. An LLM step writes a short summary per cluster, so a manager can read 5 paragraphs instead of 34K reviews.
Show it. Streamlit + Plotly and Gradio dashboards with cluster selector, top products and raw data view.
